quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Etcamah in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor approved in (09-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Etcamah (camizestrant), a once-daily oral next-generation SERD, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib) for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of an ESR1 mutation during aromatase inhibitor (AI) and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, based on an FDA-authorised test; concurrently the FDA approved a companion diagnostic test that detects emerging ESR1 mutations in circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA). The approval rests on the SERENA-6 Phase III trial (315 patients): the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 56% versus an AI plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor (HR 0.44; median PFS 16.0 versus 9.2 months), a later pre-planned analysis showed a PFS2 benefit of 25.7 versus 19.1 months (HR 0.63), and overall survival is still maturing. Recommended dose is 75mg with a CDK4/6 inhibitor. EVP Oncology Haematology Dave Fredrickson: this is the tenth FDA approval this year across AstraZeneca's portfolio and the fourth in breast cancer; the company calls it the first and only medicine of its type in the 1st-line setting (company claim). The company cites approximately 37,000 US patients with HR-positive metastatic breast cancer treated with a medicine in the 1st-line setting, approximately 30% of whom develop ESR1 mutations during 1st-line treatment before progression. Etcamah is also approved in more than 30 countries, including the EU, Japan, Canada and the UK.
